title: Grateful Dead Live at Ventura County Fairgrounds on 1982-07-17
lineage: Cassette Master (Nakamichi DR-1/Dolby B) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/96k) -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> Samplitude Professional v10.22 -> FLAC/16
source: (FOB) Sennheiser 421 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell UDXLII-C90/Dolby B)

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1982 show with a smoking Truckin' and rare China Cat > I Know You Rider combo, captured on a front‑of‑house tape that’s lively but suffers from wind‑affected mics and uneven instrument balance.
ai_review.review: The performance is marked by high energy, a standout Truckin' jam, an unusual Playing > China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider sequence and a blissful closing stretch that many reviewers call “pure bliss.”  The front‑of‑house recording (Charlie Miller/Jim Wise) delivers a warm open‑air ambience, yet wind noise, mic glitches and unbalanced levels make the sound only fair.  Overall the music outweighs the technical flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong musical performance (unique combos, high energy) combined with a decent but technically flawed audience recording yields a rating near the upper‑mid range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Wind intermittently hits microphones, short‑circuit amp noises and mic failures in set 1, instrument levels are uneven (Bobby’s guitar and Brent’s keys dominate), but the overall ambience is warm and many listeners consider it the best sounding source of this era.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set moves at a high‑energy pace but suffers from abrupt transitions—no segue between Althea and Rooster—and an oddly ending Truckin' jam, while the rare Playing > China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider sequence adds uniqueness.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals are in fine form; however his guitar sits lower in the mix due to level issues.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is noticeably quieter than other instruments, buried beneath louder guitars and keyboards.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby's guitar is unusually forward in the mix, often louder than Jerry's.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s keyboards are prominent, sometimes overpowering Phil’s bass.
band_member_comments.Drums: Nice jamming before the drums come in; overall drum work supports the high‑energy feel.
